Subject: Post-demo: EU residency + 0-retention for PII — proposed scope & next steps

Hi Anna / Liam — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align with MedInsights' privacy and legal needs.

Key points from the call:
- Requirement: EU-only data residency for all inference and logs (GDPR scope).
- Hard requirement: 0-retention for PII fields (names, SSNs, patient identifiers) — you called this non-negotiable for regulated workflows.
- Request: Ability for shortened logs (for debugging) while ensuring no PII persisted.
- Audit: your security team wants SOC 2 evidence + architecture/dataflow diagram + sample redacted logs.

Redwood proposed options (high level):
1) Route-level 0-retention policy (PII-tagged routes) — drop PII at ingress and never write to persistent logs; ephemeral KV cache only.
2) Shortened logs for non-PII telemetry (configurable window, e.g., 7–30 days) with hashing/pepper of session ids.
3) EU-only tenancy: private deployment or regional pinning on our hosted Dedicated fleet.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-options-v2.pdf (summary of options), eu-deployment-arch.png (high-level flow).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa (SE) to share a technical write-up with concrete configs and the expected tradeoffs (latency/cost).
- We’ll provide SOC 2 evidence + sample redacted logs for legal review.
- Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive next week with your security/engineering teams.

Please confirm: 1) target in-country (EU) region(s) — EU-West vs EU-Central? 2) a list of PII types you consider "PII" (so we can match redaction rules).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — good recap.

A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:
- Confirmed: all processing and logs must remain within EU data centers. Prefer EU-Central (Frankfurt) but EU-West (Ireland) is acceptable for redundancy.
- 0-retention: must apply to any field that could be used to re-identify a patient (full name, MRN, DOB, email, phone, IPs tied to accounts). We can provide a canonical list but the definitions above are a start.
- Shortened logs: acceptable for non-PII telemetry only. For debugging, we need the ability to request short-term access to ephemeral traces (audit trail) but only after an access review and with redaction.
- Proof: please send SOC 2 reports and an example of a redacted log bundle showing how prompts and responses would look after redaction/pseudonymization. Our legal team will need that for the procurement packet.

One more ask: does Redwood support automatic redaction at ingestion (regex + ML-based detectors) and can that be configured per-route? Also curious about what happens to KV caches containing sensitive tokens — are those ever persisted, and if so, for how long?

Can we do the security deep-dive with our security lead, Lucas, on Monday 15 Jun at 10:00 CEST?

Best,

Hi Anna / Liam — Marissa from Redwood SE team here. I pulled together a more concrete set of options and what we can deliver for your legal/security pack. Answers inline and then a recommended path for a pilot.

Q: automatic redaction at ingestion + route-level config?
A: Yes. Redwood supports a hybrid approach: deterministic redaction (regex) + ML detectors (PII model) at the edge ingress. Policies can be applied at the route/model level. You can tag routes as "PII_strict" which enforces 0-retention and strips or replaces any matched PII tokens before any persistence.

Q: KV cache persistence?
A: By default KV caches are in-memory per-inference worker and are ephemeral. For some dedicated/private deployments we persist short-lived caches to local SSD to improve cold-start latency; for MedInsights we propose to disable persistent KV writes for PII-tagged routes (ephemeral-only). We can also encrypt in-memory caches and add an HSM-backed key rotation schedule.

Concernts you raised and our mitigations:
- 0-retention for PII: Implemented by route policy that does not emit PII fields to logging backends. Redaction occurs at ingress and is enforced in the serving runtime (pre-serialization).
- Shortened non-PII logs: configurable retention window (7/14/30 days). Logs automatically truncate request/response fields to metadata-only (length, token counts, model id) unless explicitly allowed via a route flag.
- Auditability: we provide an "audit token" flow — a hashed, timebound token that you can request for a particular session; token issuance requires an approval workflow and is logged in an immutable audit trail (with limited retained metadata).

Evidence we can provide immediately:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and compliance pack.
- Architecture/dataflow diagram (see attached eu-deployment-arch.png).
- Sample redacted log bundle: we will generate a sanitized example showing a prompt with PII removed and session ids hashed.

Tradeoffs / cost impact:
- 0-retention for PII: negligible latency impact; increases engineering controls and monitoring (no additional per-token cost).
- Shortened logs + session hashing: small storage delta depending on retention window; we’ll produce an estimated delta after we see a 2-week sample of your traffic.

Recommended pilot plan (2–3 weeks):
1) Week 0: configure EU-Dedicated tenant (pin to EU-Central), enable route-level PII policies for 2 test routes; provide SOC 2 + architecture docs.
2) Week 1: run sample traffic (we ask for representative test set), generate redacted logs, validation run with your security team.
3) Week 2: finalize retention windows and sign off on MSA redlines for privacy addendum.

Action items for MedInsights: please share
- canonical PII list (as Anna mentioned)
- representative traffic sample (anonymized) or expected qps/token rates
- confirm the Monday deep-dive slot (15 Jun, 10:00 CEST)

I attached a concise PDF that maps the config knobs to compliance outcomes (redwood-data-retention-options-v2.pdf). We can also produce a draft privacy addendum for legal review.

Thanks — happy to jump on the Monday call and walk through the architecture.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
